known_limitations: Near-duplicate detection is lexical (tfidf). A paraphrase below the threshold is not detected, so every duplicate, leakage, and block count here is a lower bound.
manifest.json is not self-hashed. verify-release detects accidental corruption of the data, not deliberate rewriting of the manifest that describes it.
No effective sample size is quoted. It depends on an intraclass correlation, which depends on the systems being scored; manifest.dependence carries the block structure needed to compute it.
The difficulty buckets are an uncalibrated heuristic on this corpus: their ranking is not distinguishable from a random ranking of the declared tags.
license_notes: Synthetic fixture data, CC0-1.0. No real personal, clinical, or patient data.

dependence.note: effective_n is a property of a scored comparison, not of a dataset: it needs an intraclass correlation, which needs system scores. Resample these blocks, not the rows — see docs/STATISTICS.md.

card_meta.purpose: Exercise and regression-test the eval-dataset-forge audit pipeline. Every defect this corpus contains was planted deliberately and is recorded as ground truth in `defects.yaml`, so each audit stage can be scored for recall against a known answer rather than reported as a bare count. The dataset exists to make the checks falsifiable; it does not exist to measure a system.
card_meta.construction: Fourteen hand-authored English question-answer pairs, synthetic and public-safe, with nine planted defect classes: an exact duplicate, a paraphrase near-duplicate, a duplicated source record, a mislabeled answer, two ambiguous questions, a missing gold answer, conflicting annotator labels, train/test overlap, and an answer leaked into its own prompt. Splits are built by the adversarial strategy, which keeps duplicate clusters out of `dev`/`test`; examples whose gold answer is unsettled are quarantined in `train` rather than deleted. No example derives from a real person, patient, or private record.
card_meta.recommended_use: Testing dataset-audit tooling: as a fixture for this repository's test suite, as a worked example of the release format, and as a demonstration that the audit stages rediscover defects a curator planted on purpose. Read the audit findings before reading the data.
non_goals:
Not a measure of question-answering capability. Fourteen examples with three in the evaluation splits cannot distinguish two systems; the confidence interval on any score computed here spans most of the unit interval.
Not a certification that the corpus is clean. It is deliberately dirty, and the audit reports what its heuristics detect — a lower bound, never a guarantee.
Not a benchmark. It has no leaderboard, no held-out set worth holding out, and no claim to represent any task distribution.
Not medical, legal, or security guidance, and not a source of factual knowledge.
